newsitem.title: FRANCE: France needs Aerospatiale/Dassault merger - Michot.
newsitem.headline: France needs Aerospatiale/Dassault merger - Michot.

text.p: France needs a merger between aircraft companies Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation to create a group big enough to negotiate at the world level with the United States, Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot said.

U.S. aerospace giants Lockheed Martin and Northrop Grumman said on Thursday they were merging to create a group with annual sales of $37 billion, stalking the planned link-up between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp.

Minutes published on Thursday of Michot's testimony to the National Assembly defence committee on Wednesday quoted him as saying restructuring was not just a problem for Aerospatiale but one for the French nation.

"The existence of a French leader is necessary for dialogue on the European and international level with the United States. Aerospatiale, with Dassault, could on this issue present a federating role," he said.

Negotiations between Aerospatiale and Dassault were marked by a large area of agreement. They would not merge their activities but the group would have a separate branch and design office for combat planes, which would benefit from a technical exchange with Aerospatiale's design offices, he said.
The new group would have a common supervisory board and executive committee.
The capital structure for the group was a political problem which has yet to be resolved, he said.

The merger would double Aerospatiale's equity capital to 10 billion francs ($1.7 billion), but to be really competitive, it would still need a further opening of its capital to French and foreign partners, or the injection of fresh cash.

Aerospatiale, along with the other members in the Airbus Industrie consortium, believed the future of European industry lay in a single group composed of separate companies for commercial aircraft, combat planes and other programmes.

But the question of ownership of the future European group needed to be resolved as shares in Germany's Daimler-Benz AG are held in a few hands, those of British Aerospace Plc are widely dispersed, while Aerospatiale is state-owned.
"The building of a European aeronautical pole cannot be achieved with state ownership in France," he said.

Aerospatiale's strategy included linking up with defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF in missiles, and with telecommunications group Alcatel Alsthom and Thomson-CSF in satellites, he said. ($ = 5.907 French Francs)
